title: Experimental lanes orchestrator: deadman fallbacks, shadow-timestamping, and rollback rationale
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Adds an experimental "lanes" orchestrator that formalizes multi-lane rollouts (canary / A-B / shadow) with an emphasis on explainable automated rollback decisions and a deadman fallback path. Motivation: customers need a single control plane primitive to express complex multi-lane experiments while preserving predictable safety behavior under partial telemetry loss or control-plane latency. This PR implements: 1) lanes coordinator: new in-memory and persisted state machine for lanes (primary/candidate/shadow) with explicit lane transitions and timestamped shadow captures; 2) deadman fallback: if the controller cannot acquire stable telemetry for a configurable window (deadman_timeout), traffic is routed to a predetermined safe lane and an incident signal is emitted; 3) shadow-timestamping: shadow traffic is captured with request/response timestamps and trace-ids to enable precise offline replay and fidelity scoring; 4) rollback rationale: automated rollback decisions are recorded with human-readable reasons (metric anchors, drift magnitude, latency spike) and a provenance blob linking commits and rollout policy; 5) small API additions: rollout lanes extend the RolloutPolicy proto (new enum LaneType, shadow_capture_time) and rwctl gets new commands (rwctl rollout lanes status|promote|abort); 6) DB migration: rollout_lanes table to persist lane epochs, holdpoints, and last-known-reason; 7) tests and docs: integration e2e harness, unit tests for arbitration, and docs/experimental-lanes.md with examples and safety playbook. Checklist: - [x] implement lanes state machine and persistence - [x] add deadman fallback and incident hooks - [x] extend API protos and CLI - [x] migration script and backwards compatibility checks - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and example configs Notes: This is gated behind the feature flag rollout.lanes.experimental. The changes are designed to be fully backward compatible when the flag is off. See ENG-2147 for design notes and SUP-8892 for a customer reproduction that motivated the deadman behavior.

Evelyn Chen: Thanks Ravi — lowered default to 2m for hosted and introduced tiered default via config with explicit note in docs. Added fallback_invocations and shadow_capture_rate metrics in runtime. PTAL.

Nina Gomez: API change looks good. Please ensure backward-compatible wire format for rollout.proto; clients should ignore unknown enums. Also request a small compatibility test in CI that loads older rollout records.

Liam O'Connor: e2e flake observed locally — test harness replays traced requests but ordering varied; suggest deterministic seeding and a 'wait-for-metrics' helper. Also prefer the rollback rationale to include the exact metric thresholds and the sliding window used for detection.
Evelyn Chen: Introduced deterministic seed for traffic generator. Rollback rationale now includes metric window and threshold snapshot in the provenance blob (human-readable plus JSON in DB).

notes: This PR focuses on the control-plane orchestration and safety wiring; runtime sampling/efficiency improvements for shadow capture are planned in a follow-up PR (ENG-2189). The migration was designed to be idempotent and safe for rolling upgrades.
example_config:
apiVersion: v1
kind: RolloutPolicy
metadata:
  name: example-lanes
spec:
  lanes:
    - name: stable
      type: primary
    - name: candidate-v2
      type: canary
      percent: 5
    - name: shadow-v2
      type: shadow
      capture: true
      shadow_capture_time: 30s
  deadman_timeout: 2m
  holdpoints:
    - metric: latency_p95
      window: 5m
      threshold: 1.5x
